beta_new: Start up a neighbouring route to a terrace and set a belay, then shuffle thirty feet through the cave behind it to reach the far-side anchors and rappel. A very large cam is handy for the belay.

moves.from: A very large cam is handy for the belay.

beta_new: Ascend the flake, leaning on face edges to the left. A few jams near the finish gain a terrace holding the bolted anchors.
Start from a boulder and pull through the surprisingly good holds on dark stone, finishing at the anchors.

Pull through a roof into steep climbing, reaching a more upright section with an excellent shaking-out spot on a tiny shelf. The overhanging headwall comes next; aim for a faint corner high up, recover below it as best you are able, then lunge rightward and finish at the chains.
Begin on a flake, gain a shelf, then work the upright ribs until you reach a reasonable stance. One bulge remains before the anchors.
Climb the heavily featured face on bolts as far as a ledge-like break where ferns grow, about eighty feet up. Lowering from there makes a nice shorter route.
Go beyond the lower anchors, over the crux bulge and into steeper stone, finishing at the upper pair of anchors.

moves.from: Plan on a 60 m rope to lower from the top.

value.text: A 60 m rope, to lower from the top.

beta_new: Solve the bouldery opening, then cruise upward on enormous holds to the chains.
Leap into the offwidth and stay in it until it ends, then drift rightward to a pine and back leftward into the flared crack for the finish. Expect long gaps between protection.
Work up sloping holds onto a spacious shelf, then step off it into a short steeper stretch that ends at the chains.
Use the crack for a move or two, then step left onto the slim arete and its generous holds. Place your gear while still in the crack, then climb on to the spacious ledge.
A tough opening gives way to entertaining sequences, then a blank stretch higher up. A giant hueco offers a stance with a fine view at the anchors.
Step off a boulder to get started, then slap and pull your way upward using side-pulls and undercuts on the bolted wall until the chains.
Take the crack on the flake's left flank; it narrows as you approach the finish.
You can stop after the first six bolts, around 45 feet up, or keep climbing four extra bolts to the upper anchors for extra mileage.
A mixed arete where extra gear is worth carrying. Tiptoe along the arete, then step rightward onto the wall just before the end for a finale that shakes your legs.
Pass one bolt on the way to a ledge fifteen feet up, then work the slab toward a puzzling bulge close to the top.

Shuffle rightward along a slim shelf for the first clip, then follow pockets across a blank-looking stretch toward a huge cave. Hand-traverse a little rightward along the cave's lower lip, then crank over the arched roof to the chains.
Begin up the neighbouring corner route, then follow a flake that arches leftward all the way across to the anchor of another route.

The thin crack, sized for hands, pumps you out until the chimney looms and the sequence becomes unclear; plug a large cam and fight into the squeeze. Slot a bigger cam overhead when you can, then creep out to a good jam where it narrows. Fists and forearms take you to a final good jam, and from there pace yourself upward.
Large holds precede a crux on sloping holds; beyond it, kinder holds carry you to the anchors.

Descend a bit from the belay tree and traverse right, then rise to a platform under a thin crack cutting the roof. Stretch beyond the lip for reasonable holds, then let your feet swing free and crank over. Slap through long stretches to sloping pockets and twin thin cracks, layback along thin edges into a hand crack, then fire for the summit.
Four bolts lead up the left arete of the pinnacle to a big flat ledge, after which you continue to the anchors shortly before the summit. Topping out is possible from there.
Follow the hand crack until it ends at the hueco, then lower or rappel from the fixed gear.
The hand crack lives inside a stubby, dark corner; about forty feet of it ends at fixed gear for lowering.
An awkward small roof comes first; balance across its lip, then continue on the low-angled wall to a fine terrace. Give your feet a break there before the remaining stretch to the anchors.
Stand on a little boulder to start, then angle upward and leftward; a single big sloper move waits just before the anchors.
Work the slab, angle leftward onto the arete, then step up using underclings, and finish by laybacking the arete. Tougher alternatives exist if you set a top rope from the anchors.
Follow the hand-size crack up the jumbly face to the ledge, where bolted rappel anchors wait.
Climb the face beside the blunt arete and slab, drift leftward where holds thin out, then return rightward to the anchors.
Get over the low roof into the corner, then work across the bulge that resembles a turret on the way to the anchor.
Large pockets lead to the first bolt; after that, carefully poke fingers into tiny pockets to reach a resting spot near the finish. Stay focused, because the chains are still some way off.
Clipping the third bolt is the tense moment; make sure your belayer is attentive.
Enter the corridor beside the pinnacle, find the crack, and follow it to the anchors of the neighbouring route.

Ascend the corner, then underclings and jams carry you beneath the roof. Over the lip lies a second corner; turn your body sideways and scum upward until the crack widens again, then place gear and sprint toward the ledge.
Stemming is the technique for this slender corner, which faces right. Protection is found where the rock offers it, and the climb ends on a ledge.

The first moves are relatively easy up to bolt three. A bouldery leftward kick reaches a quick shake, then a harder bouldery section leads to a decent rest. The final redpoint run goes to the break, and a short finish follows.
Big pulls on sloping holds carry you to the horizontal break about twenty-five feet up. Stand up on the face over it and stay composed all the way to the anchors.
Climb the left-hand cracks into the bulge shaped like a V, get past it on its right side to gain the ledge, and lower off the fixed gear.
The steepening corner faces left; start up it, then layback until you hit anchors for rappelling, perched on a shelf above the finish of a neighbouring route.
